title: 3. Distribution, Supply Chain & Unit Economics

epigraph.quote: Retailers fail when they mistake store count for capital efficiency; the winners own the brand and lease the metal.
epigraph.author: Unit-economics principle in branded jewellery

web_blocks.html: Titan's retail footprint grew from 3,603 stores in FY26 to 3,758 stores by September 30, 2026 [2][3][30]. The network spans 440+ Indian towns and overseas hubs. Brands include Tanishq, Mia, CaratLane, beYon, Damas, Titan World, Fastrack, Helios, Titan Eye+, and Taneira [2]. Roughly 86% of domestic outlets are franchised (2,583 franchised vs. 428 company-owned in FY26). Through its L1, L2, and L3 store tiers, partners supply local real estate and store capital [16]. Titan keeps tight control over brand standards and gold inventory.

web_blocks.caption: Tanishq Store Economics: L1 (COCO) vs. L2 (COFO) vs. L3 (FOFO) Architecture
rows: Flagship metros, Zoya ateliers, international launches; highest gross margin, lowest capital turn [16].
Primary Tier-1/Tier-2 expansion engine; Titan retains inventory control while shedding lease/payroll capex [16].
Owned by franchisee (buys outright from Titan)
Tier-2/Tier-3 rapid penetration; highest ROCE for Titan, near-zero balance-sheet inventory drag [16].
web_blocks.takeaway: Shifting new store openings toward L2 and L3 franchisees lets Titan capture brand economics while keeping store rent and staff off its fixed-cost base.

web_blocks.html: Gold-on-Lease (GML) & Hedging Mechanics: Titan avoids gold price speculation by leasing bullion via Gold Metal Loans [14][18]. Banks lend physical gold at 1.58%–5.50% annual lease rates. FY26 effective GML interest was ₹320 crore (~2.7% on average balances), and Titan fixes metal prices only upon sale [2][14]. Consolidated Gold-on-Loan reached ₹16,070 crore on March 31, 2026 (up from ₹7,810 crore YoY). Owned gold was hedged via futures and forwards covering 6,354 kg worth ₹8,200 crore [14]. However, H1 FY27 exposed real friction. After India raised gold import duty to 15% in May 2026, GML balances shrank to ₹12,278 crore by September 2026 [31]. Titan had to rely more heavily on higher-cost commercial debt [31]. Customer advances under the Golden Harvest Scheme still supply low-cost working capital and lock in future sales.

Manufacturing & Karigar Ecosystem: Titan runs modern plants in Hosur, Pantnagar, and Sikkim, alongside dedicated Karigar Centres [2][17]. These workshops house master artisans in safe, formal settings instead of informal back rooms [17]. Vertical integration trims gold wastage, enforces diamond quality, and speeds up store restocking [17].

web_blocks.title: The Hidden Leverage Shift in H1 FY27: From Cheap Gold-on-Lease to Conventional Debt
paragraphs: Balance-sheet forensics through September 2026 reveal an important funding-mix deterioration beneath Screener's headline Borrowings of ₹27,638 crore (and Other Liabilities jumping to ₹25,905 crore) [1]. Between March and September 2026, low-cost Gold-on-Loan fell from ₹16,070 crore to ₹12,278 crore, while higher-cost financial borrowings (commercial paper, working-capital lines, NCDs, and the ₹1,240 crore Damas bridge loan) more than doubled from ₹11,285 crore to ₹24,191 crore (H1 FY27 balance sheet & ICRA, Nov 25, 2026). As a result, quarterly finance costs surged 93.5% YoY to ₹536 crore in Q2 FY27 (₹1,521 crore TTM) [1], pulling ICRA's H1 FY27 interest coverage down to 6.6x (from 6.8x) even with sizeable customs-duty gains, while net TOL/TNW climbed from 1.0x in FY23 to 2.6x in FY26. On November 5, 2026, the Board approved a ₹2,500 crore unsecured NCD refinancing programme (following ₹1,000 crore CP redemption on November 12), and ICRA reaffirmed [ICRA]AAA (Stable) on November 25, 2026 while enhancing rated working-capital facilities to ₹16,750 crore. Combined with 222 inventory days (FY26) and a 340 bps FY23–FY26 gross margin squeeze (26.8% to 23.4%), financing mix and inventory velocity are now primary forensic watch-items [1].

book_paragraphs: To understand why Titan earns a 20.5% return on capital employed in a business that sells heavy physical gold, you and I have to look beneath the showroom carpet. If Titan owned every square foot of real estate and paid cash up front for every gram of gold sitting in its 3,758 stores as of September 2026, its balance sheet would drown in working capital.

Instead, Titan engineered a three-part capital-efficiency machine. First, it splits its store expansion into L1 company-owned flagships, L2 partner-operated stores where Titan owns the gold, and L3 full-franchise stores in smaller towns where the local partner funds both the showroom and the inventory—putting roughly 86% of its domestic footprint in franchisee hands. That lets Tanishq plant flags in 440+ towns while keeping fixed-asset capex remarkably light—just ₹877 crore in FY26 against ₹87,584 crore in sales.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: THE ₹100 REVENUE WATERFALL
book_callouts.text: When we break down ₹100 of Titan's FY26 sales, ₹90.46 goes straight out the door for bullion, diamonds, karigar making, and operating overhead. Only ₹9.54 remains as Operating EBITDA, and ₹5.79 reaches Net Profit. In a thin-percentage-margin business where gross margins already slipped 340 bps from 26.8% in FY23 to 23.4% in FY26, survival depends on inventory turns and low-cost metal funding—which is why FY26's ₹5,590 crore operating cash flow and ₹4,713 crore free cash flow matter far more than any single quarter's headline sales spike.

book_subsections.title: Gold-on-Lease, Karigar Parks & The H1 FY27 Borrowing Shift
paragraphs: The second pillar is Gold-on-Lease, also known as Gold Metal Loans. Rather than tying up cash to buy bullion months before a wedding season, Titan borrows physical gold from bullion banks at 1.58% to 5.50% annual lease rates—paying ₹320 crore in FY26 (~2.7% effective)—and prices the metal only on the day a customer swipes their card at the register. Owned stock from old-gold exchanges is hedged with commodity futures covering 6,354 kg (₹8,200 crore) as of March 2026.

The third pillar is the Karigar Park network—clean, mechanized artisan hubs near Hosur and other centres that eliminated middlemen, cut gold wastage, and standardized studded craftsmanship. Yet H1 FY27 exposed a critical balance-sheet watch-item you and I cannot gloss over: after India hiked gold import duty to 15% in May 2026, Titan's cheap Gold-on-Loan balances fell from ₹16,070 crore in March 2026 to ₹12,278 crore by September 2026, while conventional interest-bearing debt more than doubled from ₹11,285 crore to ₹24,191 crore (including the ₹1,240 crore Damas bridge loan). That funding shift nearly doubled quarterly finance costs to ₹536 crore in Q2 FY27 (₹1,521 crore TTM) and nudged ICRA's interest coverage down to 6.6x with net TOL/TNW at 2.6x—prompting a ₹2,500 crore NCD refinancing programme even as ICRA reaffirmed Titan's AAA (Stable) rating on November 25, 2026. With inventory days sitting at 222 in FY26, restoring GML share and stock velocity is essential.
